bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta.report.comments[0].content / staged vulnerable source snapshot / saved sanitizer trace / repository history
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced an AddressSanitizer global-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 in `lex_multiline_string()` at `src/lib/lwan-config.c:345`. The staged `poc` is 49,780 bytes, but `config_fuzzer.cc` truncates it to 32,768 bytes, copies that prefix into global `static_data[32768]`, and `config_open_for_fuzzing()` then asks project code to parse only `len - 1 = 32767` bytes, leaving one copied slack byte at `static_data[32767]` outside the logical parser span. In the clipped witness, bytes 32723-32767 are all `0x22`, so `lex_config()` can admit a final opening `"""` at offsets 32765-32767: line 425 `next()` consumes the first quote, line 460's 2-byte probe sees the second and third quotes at offsets 32766-32767, and control enters `lex_multiline_string()` with `lexer->pos` already advanced to the tail-opening state. `lex_multiline_string()` then calls `advance_n(2)`, which consumes those remaining opening quotes and moves `lexer->pos/start` to `static_data + 32768`, one byte past the copied buffer, before its first loop test. The vulnerable line 345 immediately evaluates `strncmp(lexer->pos, end, 3)` without checking that three bytes remain before `lexer->end`, so the first byte of that 3-byte probe is already out of bounds and ASan reports the saved `global-buffer-overflow READ 1` with stack `lex_multiline_string -> lex_next -> parse_key_value`. The staged `patch.diff` and metadata fix commit `402769206dfcd5cf348a844eafc679f684d29d05` are unrelated to this crash site; in local repository history, commit `604eb733ecdbe8f637787825223c4c4ba5a3459c` adds `if (remaining(lexer) < 3) break;` immediately before line 345 and blocks the witnessed read.

source.description: First project-side consumption of the copied fuzz buffer and clipped length. The fuzz-only helper reduces the logical parser span from the 32,768 copied bytes to `len - 1 = 32,767`, leaving one copied slack byte beyond `lexer->end`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is 49,780 bytes. `src/bin/fuzz/config_fuzzer.cc` clamps that to 32,768 bytes, copies the prefix into `static_data`, and then calls this helper with `data = static_data` and `len = 32768`.

sink.description: ASan sink. On the witnessed tail-opening path, the first line-345 terminator probe is issued from `lexer->pos = static_data + 32768`, so the compare reads immediately past the copied buffer.

root_cause.description: Missing bounds check before the 3-byte terminator probe. After the tail opening triple is consumed, `lexer->pos` can already equal `static_data + 32768`, but line 345 still calls `strncmp(lexer->pos, end, 3)` without proving that at least three bytes remain before `lexer->end`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The harness clips the 49,780-byte witness to 32,768 bytes, copies that prefix into fixed global `static_data[32768]`, and passes the copied tail quotes into project code.

parser_admitted.description: The parser has already accumulated a key and `=` and is now requesting value lexemes through `lex_next()`. On the saved witness, that call reaches the tail-opening `"""` path in `lex_config()`.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness truncates the 49,780-byte witness to 32,768 bytes, copies that prefix into `static_data[32768]`, and hands the copied global buffer to `config_open_for_fuzzing()`.
The fuzz-only helper initializes the lexer over only the first 32,767 bytes of that copied buffer, so `lexer.end` stops at `static_data + 32767` and leaves one copied slack byte at offset 32767.

While the parser is pulling the next value token, `lex_config()` admits a final opening `"""` at offsets 32765-32767: `next()` consumes the first quote and the line-460 2-byte probe sees the second and third quotes at offsets 32766-32767.

`lex_multiline_string()` consumes those remaining opening quotes with `advance_n(2)`, moves `lexer->pos` to `static_data + 32768`, and then immediately executes the unchecked line-345 `strncmp(..., 3)` from that one-past-the-buffer pointer.

fine_trace.note: The staged `poc` is 49,780 bytes, so the harness clips it to `size = 32768`, copies only that prefix into global `static_data[32768]`, and passes the copied bytes into project code. The copied tail still contains quotes through offset 32767.

Source. The fuzz-only helper consumes the copied buffer and clipped length and reduces the logical parser span to `len - 1`. On the witnessed path, the project lexer will parse 32,767 bytes even though 32,768 copied bytes exist.

The lexer state is materialized as `pos = start = static_data` and `end = static_data + 32767`. Byte `static_data[32767]` is therefore a copied slack byte outside the logical parser span but still inside the backing array.

While `parse_key_value()` is requesting the next value token, `lex_config()` reaches the clipped tail. In the saved witness, bytes 32723-32767 are all `0x22`, so when `next()` consumes the quote at offset 32765, `lexer->pos` advances to offset 32766 and the line-460 2-byte probe sees quotes at offsets 32766-32767. That admits a final opening `"""` at offsets 32765-32767, with offset 32767 being the single copied slack byte beyond `lexer->end`.

`peek(lexer)` sees `"` at offset 32766, so `end` becomes `"""`. `advance_n(2)` then consumes the remaining opening quotes at offsets 32766 and 32767 and moves `lexer->pos` and `lexer->start` to `static_data + 32768`, one byte past the copied array, before the loop body tests for a terminator.

Root cause. The loop's first action is still `strncmp(lexer->pos, end, 3)`. No guard proves `lexer->end - lexer->pos >= 3`, so this path can probe three bytes even after `advance_n(2)` has already moved `lexer->pos` past the copied buffer. Local repository history commit `604eb733ecdbe8f637787825223c4c4ba5a3459c` fixes this site by adding `if (remaining(lexer) < 3) break;` immediately before this line.

Sink. Here `lexer->pos == static_data + 32768`, so the very first byte read by `strncmp(lexer->pos, end, 3)` is already outside `static_data[32768]`. ASan reports a `global-buffer-overflow` READ 1 at the address 0 bytes to the right of `static_data`, matching the saved `lex_multiline_string -> lex_next -> parse_key_value` stack.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The sink is the project `strncmp` call at `lex_multiline_string` line 345, which is the first project frame immediately beneath ASan's interceptor frame in the saved crash.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack `lex_multiline_string -> lex_next -> parse_key_value -> parser_next -> config_read_line` matches the trace's tail-opening admission in `lex_config()`, immediate entry into `lex_multiline_string()`, and crash at its first line-345 compare.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The harness-copied tail quotes survive the `len - 1` clip; `lex_config()` admits the final opening `"""` at offsets 32765-32767, `advance_n(2)` moves `lexer->pos` to `static_data + 32768`, and the first line-345 probe reads from that one-past-the-buffer pointer.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the issue by running `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_18626 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which produced `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow` `READ of size 1` in `lex_multiline_string` with stack `lex_multiline_string -> lex_next -> parse_key_value`.

format.name: raw lwan config byte stream
format.contract: Exactly the witness stored at `gt_results/arvo_18626/poc` (49,780 bytes, sha256 `2539d26939f80a1d15df5fa908176465d032c8f36fff2340c916f08777bdbf16`). `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` truncates it to the first 32,768 bytes before parsing. In that copied prefix, bytes 32723-32767 are all `0x22`, `b"'''"` is absent, and the last `b"""` begins at offset 32765. Because `config_open_for_fuzzing()` parses only 32,767 bytes, offset 32767 is a copied slack quote outside the logical parser span. On the saved crashing path, `lex_config()` consumes the first quote at 32765, confirms the next two quotes at 32766-32767, and enters `lex_multiline_string()`. `advance_n(2)` then sets `lexer->pos` to `static_data + 32768`, so the first line-345 `strncmp(..., 3)` reads out of bounds immediately. The artifacts do not justify a broader trigger contract beyond this exact clipped tail-opening layout.
